label: 09:30 FINAL MORNING
houseNoteTopic: PQ1 lounge poker route to Bains
story: The runner put the new sheet on the Delphoria counter with the fold still in it. The clerk pulled yesterday’s copy off the nail and slid this one under the scarred glass. Three LEAN slips. No BET. From the lounge came the scrape of a chair; from behind the other door, cards being dealt. The Sports Desk kept its own hours.

Jesse’s name reached the bartender before Jesse reached the room. A regular started asking which of the three had money behind it. The bartender looked toward the door and stopped answering. Jesse read the calls once. ‘Interested isn’t in.’ The clerk left the cash drawer shut and pinned the three slips where a runner could find them.

The second copy had five numbers circled. That one went toward the worn elevator. Nobody crossed out the PASS stamps to make the page look better. At the private-room door the runner waited until Jesse held out his hand. ‘Give me the sheet. Leave the sales pitch downstairs.’
noBetLine: Three to watch. Nothing to collect.

edgeStory: The clerk tapped the second line, the college total, and asked whether a plus sign was enough. Jesse put a finger on its PASS stamp. ‘Read the whole slip.’ The last three comparisons were below zero. They stayed on the file because these were the five highest on the sheet, not five promises.

A caller wanted the Carolina puck line because the price looked generous. The runner read him the call, not the headline payout. PASS. The receiver went back on its hook. Upstairs, the five circled numbers had bought five lines of attention and not a dollar of action.
houseNote: In Police Quest’s Hotel Delphoria sequence, Sonny Bonds reaches Bains through the lounge’s illegal gambling operation and poker game. The lounge is the way into the back room, not a respectable guest amenity. That is the route this sheet belongs to: counter, cards, then the man everybody has been careful not to interrupt.
backRoom: The poker game did not stop for a zero-stake sports sheet. A player squared his cards while the runner laid the carbon copy beside Jesse. The chips already on the table belonged to that game; the report had created no new sports action.

Outside the private room, somebody tried to revive a better number from an old slip. The clerk had already taken that copy off the counter. ‘Bring what’s on the sheet,’ Jesse said. One sentence. The runner folded the old page without asking another question.

This edition stays pinned until the next deliberate Hotline update. A later report, a new price or a finished game does not silently rewrite the copy in your hand. Check the issue stamp before carrying it upstairs.
lastWord: Three LEANs on the nail. Five comparisons in the file. No BET on the sheet. Jesse handed the copy back. ‘Keep the phone clear.’
